messages:
Aisha (PM): Quick sync — customer ‘BrightPay’ is pushing for guaranteed preheat (grace window prewarm) during scheduled payroll peaks. They want a contract clause: 1h prewarm before peak + <250ms p95 latency. Can we scope this for Dedicated?
Pranav (Eng): TL;DR: feasible but costy. Prewarming a pool for 1h at steady-state means reserved GPUs idle some fraction. Need rules for when to start/stop prewarm and backfill behavior.
Maya (Product): Important to separate two asks: (1) contractual SLA for latency during window, (2) UX to schedule prewarm windows and surface cost. We should handle them as distinct workstreams.
Jonah (SRE): Ops concerns: what happens when capacity used elsewhere? We need soft-spill rules and a fallback model variant (smaller quantized model). Otherwise we risk evicting prewarm and breaking SLA.
Ben (Ops): Also need billing clarity: how do we charge for idle prewarm time vs reserved capacity? Do we bill full reserved rate or a prewarm add-on? Finance wants a clear metric.
Aisha (PM): Proposed scope for MVP: - Schedule UI + API for prewarm window - Autoscale policy to respect scheduled windows with hard preemption guard - Fallback to quantized model when we can’t satisfy prewarm. Launch criteria below?
Tara (CS): Customer success note: BrightPay will only sign if they get a simple contract line: guaranteed peak latency OR credit. They prefer guaranteed latency. They asked for a pilot next month.
Pranav (Eng): Autoscale sketch (P0 experiment):
```
- prewarm_start = window_start - prewarm_lead (configurable, default 30m)
- target_capacity = max(steady_demand, scheduled_headroom)
- scale_up_rate = ramp/sec (avoid instant allocations)
- eviction_policy: only evict opportunistic (spot) first, then soft-evict non-SLA pools
```
We need to pick defaults: prewarm_lead 30m, can be 60m for paid addon.
Maya (Product): Launch criteria (suggested MVP):
- API + Console scheduling for prewarm windows
- Autoscale respects scheduled headroom and can allocate within region
- Observable metric: prewarm_hit_rate >= 90% (requests served from warmed pool)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for 95% of scheduled windows
- Billing + contract language drafted
Aisha (PM): Cost guardrails: prewarm should be opt-in per-reservation. For pilots we can offer discounted prewarm hours. Need a telemetry runbook to measure cost delta per-customer.
Jonah (SRE): Also add an incident playbook: if prewarm fails (allocation timeout > 5m before window), auto-rollback to fallback model + issue page alert. ops-bot can create an incident if failures exceed threshold.
ops-bot: Scheduled reminder: "Prewarm pilot alert window for BrightPay on 1789000000" (automated).
Ben (Ops): One more constraint: regional capacity. If we can’t place warm instances in the same AZ due to spot pressure, we should allow cross-AZ warm or notify customer. That impacts latency — include region fallback in contract.
Tara (CS): Re customer ask: they want an SLA clause about notification lead time when we cannot meet scheduled prewarm. Suggest 30m notification + credit formula.
Pranav (Eng): Implementation risks: - Overprovisioning causing overall cluster pressure - Complex scheduling plus canary release if fallback model changes semantics
- KV cache cold-starts for chat sessions even after prewarm (need to prepopulate common prefixes?)
Maya (Product): Proposal to reduce risk: run a 2-week alpha pilot with BrightPay as follows:
- Limit pilot to 2 regions (us-west-2 + eu-west-1)
- Prewarm lead = 30m default, configurable to 60m for BrightPay
- Use quantized fallback model that’s functionally equivalent for payroll tasks
- Expose cost dashboard to BrightPay during pilot
Aisha (PM): Owners and next steps:
- Pranav: design autoscale policy + prewarm scheduler (P0) — due EOW for prototype
- Ben: billing/contract language draft (cost model) — due Tue
- Jonah: runbook + alerting + ops-bot hook — due Thu
- Maya/Tara: customer pilot playbook + kickoff with BrightPay — schedule this week
Pranav (Eng): One technical ask: do we want to implement prefix-level warm (prepopulate KV cache) or just warm hosts? Cache warm is trickier but cheaper for latency. Need perf numbers.
Jonah (SRE): We can simulate by replaying a sample of recent traffic into a warm instance during prewarm. That’d be part of the alpha.
Aisha (PM): Decision call: for MVP we do host prewarm only (no automatic prefix seeding). If alpha shows cache misses cause >10% latency regression, promote prefix seeding to P1.
Maya (Product): Agree. Also log requirements: token-level cost for prewarm hours, p95 latency histograms, prewarm_hit_rate, allocation_time. These are needed for billing + SLA proofs.
Ben (Ops): Billing formula suggestion: bill reserved rate for base capacity + prewarm addon billed hourly at X% of reserved. For pilot we can set X=30%. Finance will counter-propose.
Tara (CS): BrightPay asks for 3 pilot windows next month to validate. I’ll schedule and share traffic profiles.
Aisha (PM): Ok final notes: treat prewarm as opt-in add-on; require explicit customer approval to put SLAs in contract. We’ll run alpha -> measure -> refine launch criteria.
Pranav (Eng): I’ll open an RFC with the autoscale policy draft and sample config.
Maya (Product): I’ll add this to roadmap board: "prewarm scheduling & quota shaping (alpha)" and tag customer pilot.
Aisha (PM): Thanks all — sync follow-ups in calendar. :thumbsup:
